\section*{Multiple Choice (10 marks)}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item Gavin has two rocks. Both rocks are made up \duallayerbox{entirely of the same mineral}{from the same location}. What other
property of his two rocks is most likely to be the same?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item size
    \item shape
    \item color
    \item weight
\end{enumerate}
\item Which is an example of a \duallayerbox{human-made}{natural} product?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item cake
    \item tomato
    \item wheat
    \item coal
\end{enumerate}
\item Sulfur (S), oxygen (O2), water (H2O), and sodium chloride (NaCl) are all examples of pure
substances. Which of the following describes all pure substances?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item A pure substance consists of only one type of element.
    \item A pure substance has a definite chemical composition.
    \item A pure substance cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
    \item A pure substance is normally found as a solid at room temperature.
\end{enumerate}
\item The \duallayerbox{speed of a sound wave}{speed of light} varies as it travels through different substances. Which factor
will most affect the speed of a sound wave?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item the frequency of the wave
    \item the wavelength of the wave
    \item the source that created the sound
    \item the distance between molecules in the medium
\end{enumerate}
\item A lizard species mostly eats fruit from one particular type of tree. If a virus kills most
these trees, which individual lizards will most likely survive?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item lizards that can climb higher in the fruit trees
    \item lizards that have darker coloration
    \item lizards that can find other types of food
    \item lizards that produce more offspring
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\section*{True / False (10 marks)}
\textit{Answer True or False}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\setcounter{enumi}{5}
\item True or False: Heat transferred through the ice cube by \duallayerbox{convection}{conduction} caused it to melt on the warm sidewalk.
\item True or False: Picking up broken glass pieces \duallayerbox{by hand}{with gloves} is the best way to ensure safety during cleanup.
\item True or False: A proton is \duallayerbox{not a fundamental component}{a key component} of an atom and can be found outside the nucleus.
\item True or False: Windmills are often built in \duallayerbox{forests}{open plains} to help protect them from strong winds and storms.
\item True or False: The magnetic force on an object will \duallayerbox{remain the same}{change} regardless of the distance from the magnet.
\end{enumerate}

\section*{Long Form Response (20 marks)}
\textit{Answer each question with a clear and complete explanation.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\setcounter{enumi}{10}
\item Discuss the impact of \duallayerbox{deforestation and land burning}{urbanization} for agriculture on Earth's
atmosphere, including specific consequences for climate and air quality.
\item Discuss how the \duallayerbox{freezing temperature}{boiling point} of water allows it to exist in two different forms on
Earth, and analyze the significance of these forms in our environment.
\end{enumerate}
